main_statements.label: Theorem 1
main_statements.quantifiers: forall integer m>=1, forall complex u in H^m
limits: Scalar vanishing is proved on every complex H^m input using the analytic physical even Hamiltonian extension, compatible with the original higher-regularity hierarchy.

Both clauses hold on all original complex H^m inputs with the independently constructed K_m on complex H^(m-1), including m=1. Its actual Frechet gradient is constructed on that native domain; Gardner differentiation is the genuine physical distribution derivative.
The literal physical Hill trace at r^2 has all-order real-axis estimates with odd phase coefficients 2*K_m.

The independent actual Hill root and primitive agree with the NLS root and primitive on the full real H1 domain at nonreal frequencies with Re z>0. Exact physical trace and energy derivative identities and complex H1 source analyticity on the source-continuation domain are proved. Full labeled gap/action identification and mKdV spectral Hamiltonians remain open.

The physical H1 Miura potential has its literal Fourier coefficient map into L2. The actual L2 Hill operator spectrum and characteristic multiplicities are identified with the original NLS periodic spectrum under squaring. Exact fixed endpoint/gap-index comparisons are proved on real H1. Full spectral action and Hamiltonian identification remains open.

dependency_labels.label: Lemma 3
dependency_labels.quantifiers: All original complex H1 inputs for spectral sets and analytic multiplicities; all conjugate-reflected real H1 inputs for nonnegativity, intrinsic labels, central endpoints and every natural index n>=1 in the fixed endpoint and gap identities.
limits: Every actual H2 Hill eigenvalue condition is equivalent to the original ZS periodic spectral condition at squared frequency, including zero.
At nonzero frequency the energy characteristic order is the original ZS algebraic multiplicity; at zero the frequency multiplicity is exactly twice the energy order.
The intrinsic ordered real Hill labels have the exact characteristic zero set and analytic multiplicities and are nonnegative.

Every fixed positive Hill endpoint is the square of the corresponding original canonical NLS endpoint; the central Hill endpoint is the square of either central NLS endpoint. Closed gaps are exact square images and collapse simultaneously. The printed geometric-eigenspace multiplicity comparison remains open. No action-integral comparison is asserted.
